title: SRE weekly update 2026-04-04
content:
SRE Weekly Update - 2026-04-04

TL;DR
- Two incidents this week: a short-lived spike in token latency on hosted-api (Sev2, 2026-04-01) and a degraded KV-cache hit rate affecting low-latency customers (Sev3, 2026-04-03).
- SLOs: Hosted API p95 latency slipped to 210ms on 2026-04-01 (target p95 <= 150ms) during the spike; overall weekly availability remains at 99.98%.
- On-call: Handoffs and runbook updates completed; rotating on-call for next week: Aisha -> Marco.
- Action items: follow-up RCA for token-latency spike, add an additional Canary for front-door routing, update KV-cache monitoring alerts and paging thresholds.

INCIDENTS
1) INC-2026-0401: hosted-api token latency spike (Sev2)
- Timeline: 2026-04-01 14:03 UTC — 14:42 UTC
- Impact: p95 token generation latency rose from baseline ~120ms to peak ~420ms for ~25 minutes; increased timeouts for some short-lived requests; error rates remained low (<=0.5%).
- Detection: alerted by p95 latency alert (pager fired) and customer Slack message from a critical account.
- Mitigation: rolled back recent routing weight change to fallback model variant and activated regional fallback policy; autoscaler increased dedicated inference workers which reduced queueing.
- Root cause (candidate): an unexpected combo of degraded kernel performance after a GPU driver update and a routing change that pushed more short-sequence traffic to a worker pool tuned for long sequences.
- Immediate follow-ups: pin driver version on affected pool, revert the routing policy change in staging and validate canary, add metric to detect sequence-length distribution shifts.
- Owners: Emily Chen (mitigation lead), Priya Kapoor (customer comms), infra-team for driver rollback.

2) INC-2026-0403: KV-cache hit-rate degradation (Sev3)
- Timeline: 2026-04-03 09:10 UTC — 2026-04-03 11:30 UTC
- Impact: KV-cache hit rate dropped from ~78% to ~45% for a subset of dedicated customers, increasing per-token compute and tail latency for those workloads. No data loss; primarily cost and latency degradation for affected accounts.
- Detection: automated cache-hit SLO alert; SLO dashboard showed degradation for two dedicated clusters.
- Mitigation: cleared corrupted prefix caches, rolled cache eviction policy back to previous stable config, and throttled non-critical background traffic to reduce cache churn.
- Root cause: config rollforward (eviction thresholds) applied to a subset of clusters without proper canary. The new eviction behavior increased churn for small-session workloads.
- Follow-ups: enforce canary on cache config changes, create automated pre-deploy simulation for cache churn, schedule a postmortem doc.
- Owners: Marco Ruiz (lead), infra-config team.

SLO & METRICS
- Availability: weekly aggregate 99.98% (target 99.95% for hosted-api public endpoints) — meeting target.
- Latency: weekly p95 = 145ms but spike on 2026-04-01 pushed p95 for that day to 210ms (target daily p95 <= 150ms).
- Errors: API error rate remained low at 0.09% (target <= 0.2%).
- KV-cache hit-rate SLO for dedicated clusters: target 75% — observed 66% for the affected clusters during degradation window.
- Notes: We saw a small but measurable shift in sequence-length distribution on 2026-04-01 around 14:00 UTC — correlates with a partner job that had a large batch of short-sequence requests.

ON-CALL & HANDOFFS
- This week on-call: 2026-03-30 -> 2026-04-05: Aisha Patel (primary), Daniel Walker (secondary).
- Next week on-call: 2026-04-06 -> 2026-04-12: Marco Ruiz (primary), Emily Chen (secondary).
- Handoff notes: Aisha completed a 10-minute async handoff covering the token latency incident, steps taken, and live dashboards. Updated runbook pages: "hosted-api-latency-spike" and "kv-cache-eviction-rollbacks".
- Pager changes: lowered paging threshold for KV-cache hit-rate to reduce time-to-detect for clusters with >1000 requests/min.

RUNBOOKS & PLAYBOOKS
- Updated: hosted-api-latency-spike (added rollback checklist for routing changes), kv-cache-eviction-rollbacks (added steps to clear prefix caches safely).
- To do: add preflight checklist for kernel/driver upgrades; add recommended canary sizes for cache config changes.

ACTION ITEMS & FOLLOW-UPS (owners + ETA)
- Emily Chen: Complete RCA for INC-2026-0401 and publish postmortem (ETA 2026-04-09).
- Marco Ruiz: Implement canary enforcement for cache-config changes + automated simulation (ETA 2026-04-16).
- Infra team (lead: Priya Kapoor): Pin GPU driver version across affected pools and prepare a safe upgrade plan (ETA 2026-04-11).
- Observability (lead: Daniel Walker): Add sequence-length distribution metric and alert when shift >10% from baseline (ETA 2026-04-08).
- On-call docs: Update handoff checklist to include a short summary template and links to active incidents (ETA 2026-04-07).

MAINTENANCE & UPCOMING WORK
- Planned: Upgrade canary cluster with new autoscaler configuration (2026-04-10) — will run low-impact tests and monitor p95/p99.
- Planned: KV-cache eviction policy experiment to run in isolated staging during week of 2026-04-13.
- Reminder: coordinate with product on any planned partner batch jobs that may skew sequence distribution (reach out to Partner Growth).

RISKS & CONCERNS
- Risk: Driver upgrades without adequate perf can cause transient latency spikes. Mitigation: stricter canary policy for infra-level changes.
- Risk: config rollouts for cache eviction and routing have high blast radius if not canaried; prioritize automation to reduce human error.

MEETING NOTES / DISCUSSIONS
- Weekly SRE sync (2026-04-02): discussed the latency spike RCA hypothesis and agreed on immediate pin for driver versions + extra telemetry. Decided to add a small canary for routing weight changes (10% traffic for 30 min).
- Post-incident blameless review scheduled for 2026-04-08 16:00 UTC (invite sent to SRE, infra-config, product-eng).

ATTACHMENTS / REFERENCES
- Linked artifacts: JIRA-SRE-4212 (incident tracking), CONFLUENCE-SRE-ONCALL-HANDOFF (updated handoff template), PR #987 (infra config rollback).

If you have questions or need context before the postmortem, ping in #sre-incident or DM me (Daniel).

- Daniel
